quote: I am therefore confident in dismissing psychic powers as a priori implausible, despite all the claimed experimental evidence in favor of them.
content: Three years later the claimed experimental evidence got its best test, and the outcome supports the essay in a way that reaches further than the essay intended. Bem’s “Feeling the Future” (Bem (2011)) reported nine experiments showing precognition, in the field’s flagship journal, using the standard methods of experimental social psychology. Direct replications failed (Ritchie, Wiseman & French (2012); Galak et al. (2012)), and the methodological response (Wagenmakers et al. (2011)) argued that the right conclusion was not that Bem had cheated but that the methods which produced his result, flexible analysis, optional stopping, one-sided tests and a publication process that accepts them, were the ordinary methods of the discipline, and would produce “evidence” for anything. That argument is the one this essay makes about priors, and it became a founding document of the replication crisis. The consequence the book does not draw is that the same prior-based dismissal applies to the effects the book’s own essays cite from the same journals by the same methods; the essays on scarcity, anchoring, priming and conformity were annotated in Books II and IV with the results of applying it.

quote: Which just goes to say: The existence of psychic powers is a privileged probabilistic assertion of non-reductionist worldviews—they own that advance prediction; they devised it and put it forth, in defiance of reductionist expectations.
content: The likelihood ratio here is asserted, not derived, and the history does not support the ownership claim. Cartesian interactionism, the paradigm non-reductionist theory, predicts nothing about mind-to-mind links: each soul interacts with its own pineal gland, and telepathy would need a further law that Descartes never posited. The people who actually “devised and put forth” psi as a research programme, from the Society for Psychical Research through Rhine to the Ganzfeld researchers, mostly framed it in quasi-physical terms, fields, radiation, quantum entanglement, and the modern parapsychological literature is, if anything, more attached to physicalist mechanisms than to souls. So the advance prediction was made by a mixed group, for reasons that had little to do with the ontological status of belief, and what the essay is really saying is that psi would be evidence for something the current picture excludes, which is true and much weaker. The essay’s opening concession to Fallenstein (“You’re right”) is the best thing in it: an overreach in the previous essay, that irreducibility could never be confirmed, corrected within a day. The rest of the essay then rebuilds the confident conclusion on a likelihood ratio it does not compute.
